title: Codebase Understanding Database — Overview and definition
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Symbol indexes, dependency maps, architecture descriptions, and call graphs for codebases. The Codebase Understanding Database turns an unfamiliar codebase into a navigable map: every symbol indexed, every dependency mapped, the architecture described in plain language, and call graphs showing how execution flows. Onboarding to a million-line codebase normally takes months; these records compress it to hours by answering 'what does this do, what calls it, what does it depend on' for any symbol in the tree.
capabilities: Symbol indexes: definitions, references, and documentation per symbol
Dependency maps: module-to-module and package-level graphs
Architecture descriptions: layers, boundaries, and data flow in plain language
Call graphs: who calls whom, with hot paths highlighted
Change-impact analysis: what breaks if this symbol changes

title: Codebase Understanding Database — Knowledge: technical reference
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Index anatomy: symbols (functions, classes, variables) with {name, kind, file, line, signature, doc}; references (every use site); dependencies (imports/requires per module, resolved to targets). Call graph: directed edges caller->callee; static analysis resolves direct calls; dynamic calls marked approximate. Architecture recovery: cluster modules by dependency density; layers emerge from the DAG of dependencies; entry points are nodes with no incoming edges from inside the tree. Impact analysis: reverse-reachability from the changed symbol gives the affected set; intersect with test coverage for the test plan. Metrics: fan-in/fan-out per symbol, cyclic dependency detection, dead-code candidates (zero incoming references).

demo.title: Execution: build pipeline generate-build-test-fix
demo.code: let attempts=0;function build(code){attempts++;return code.includes('BUG')?{ok:false,log:'compile error: BUG token'}:{ok:true,log:'build clean'};}let code='v1 with BUG';let res=build(code);while(!res.ok&&attempts<5){code=code.replace('BUG','FIX');res=build(code);}J({attempts,ok:res.ok,log:res.log});assert(res.ok&&attempts===2,'buildloop');

demo.title: Verification: property-based test of sort
demo.code: function prop(a){const s=[...a].sort((x,y)=>x-y);const sorted=s.every((v,i)=>i===0||s[i-1]<=v);const perm=JSON.stringify([...a].sort((x,y)=>x-y))===JSON.stringify(s);return sorted&&perm;}let seed=42;function rnd(){seed=(seed*1103515245+12345)&0x7fffffff;return seed%100;}let pass=true;for(let t=0;t<200;t++){const a=Array.from({length:10},rnd);if(!prop(a)){pass=false;break;}}J({trials:200,pass});assert(pass,'property');

title: Codebase Understanding Database — Verification: tests and limitations
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Tests: index-completeness test (every defined symbol indexed); reference test (known call sites all found); cycle test (known cycles detected); impact test (affected set matches manual analysis on the sample). Limitations: dynamic languages need runtime data for full graphs; generated code inflates indexes (flagged); very large trees need incremental indexing. Indexes carry the indexed commit/version.

demo.title: Execution: debugging signature match and bisection
demo.code: const sigs=[{re:/index out of range/i,cause:'off-by-one'},{re:/null|undefined/i,cause:'null-deref'}];const err='IndexError: list index out of range';const m=sigs.find(s=>s.re.test(err));const commits=['c1','c2','c3','c4','c5','c6','c7','c8'];const bad=5;let lo=0,hi=commits.length-1,steps=0;while(lo<hi){steps++;const mid=(lo+hi)>>1;if(mid>=bad)hi=mid;else lo=mid+1;}J({cause:m.cause,culprit:commits[lo],steps});assert(m.cause==='off-by-one'&&commits[lo]==='c6'&&steps===3,'debug');
